title: A worker that succeeds without writing a report is reported as BLOCKED and told to re-dispatch
description:
Same live run, same tick (run_215b7cbff9dd405c80d738be45cccde5, tick 5jo). The container's own facts line and the report it generated contradict each other:

  _ticks-worker: branch tick/72y/5jo, base 16a0d262, harness omp exited 0, 2 work commit(s), 0 uncommitted path(s)._
  ...
  STATUS: BLOCKED — the harness exited 0 and wrote no report; re-dispatch this tick

Exit 0 and two real work commits is a SUCCESS. The agent simply never wrote RESULT-5jo.md, which the prompt calls 'the ONLY channel'. The fallback report then recommends the single most wasteful possible action — re-dispatching a tick whose work already landed and is sitting on the branch.

The fallback itself is right to exist and tick 5fg's salvage is right to keep the work; the defect is that one shape ('no report, nothing landed') and a very different shape ('no report, work landed and the harness exited clean') collapse into the same verdict and the same advice. That is the failure mode .tick/learnings.md already names: never collapse distinct failure classes into one message.

What the fallback should distinguish, using facts the entrypoint already has in hand:
- exit != 0, no commits            -> BLOCKED, re-dispatch. Today's message, correct.
- exit == 0, work commits present  -> the work landed and is reviewable; the agent's account is MISSING. Do not advise re-dispatch; advise reviewing the branch, and say plainly that no agent report exists.
- exit != 0, work commits present  -> partial, salvaged (5fg's path); name both facts.

Related and worth checking in the same pass: tick gm5 covers a report written to the wrong directory. If the agent DID write a report somewhere other than the worktree root, this tick's symptom and gm5's are the same event — confirm which happened here before designing the fix.
acceptance_criteria: A worker whose harness exits 0 with work commits but no agent report produces a status that does not say BLOCKED and does not advise re-dispatch, and names the missing report as the actual gap. Pinned by tests over the three exit/commit combinations.
